text:
anya: quick heads-up — after onboarding rankflow-v2 int4 we see a small but consistent MRR drop on prod-like holdouts (~0.018). curious if priming templates combined with quantization is the culprit.

mike: can you paste the holdout slice and the exact eval command you used?

anya: sure — short queries slice (~under 8 tokens). eval command:```python
# run eval harness
python -m evals.run --model rankflow-v2:int4 --holdout shortqueries --metrics ndcg@10,mrr --seed 42 --bootstrap 1000
```

sanjay: did you run float16 baseline with the same seeds? int4 can nudge logits especially on short context. also check candidate order/dedupe.

eva: also check priming length — our priming adds a 6-token header. if tokenization/kvcache packing differs after quant, that could change ranking. try removing priming as an ablation.

anya: yeah i ran float16 yesterday — baseline mrr=0.312, int4 mrr=0.294 on that slice. p~0.02 with bootstrap. i posted the raw csv here: https://internal.gdrive/redwood/rankflow_v2_int4_shortslice.csv

mike: that delta is small but consistent. before we over-index on quantization, let's rule out dataset and candidate order: can you run two quick ablations — (A) same eval but strip priming, (B) shuffle candidate order per query seed — see if delta persists.

julian: candidate dedupe check: if int4 scoring is slightly less stable, ties could be broken differently when order matters. add tie-breaking deterministic sort key in the scorer for one run.

anya: will spawn three jobs now (A,B,C where C is float16 for control with tie-fix). scheduling in eval queue. job ids: 9765,9766,9767 (ci-bot should pick up).

ci-bot: jobs queued: 9765 (strip-priming), 9766 (shuffle-candidates), 9767 (float16-tiefix). estimated runtime ~45m. I'll post results when done. :robot_face:

mike: thanks — also note down exact sample counts and seeds so we can reproduce the p-values in the PR. small p-values can be brittle on short slices.

eva: if ablation shows priming is the issue, my guess is the priming tokens change tokenization boundary so embeddings for short queries shift more under quant noise. we should test tokenized-length-aware quant profiles.

sanjay: another quick check: run with logits temperature=0.0 (deterministic) and with the usual temp to see if instability is score-related.

anya: noted — adding temp=0.0 runs as 9768. will share results here.

ci-bot: job 9765 finished. results: ndcg@10 delta -0.003 (ns), mrr delta -0.005 (ns). raw: https://internal.gdrive/redwood/9765_results.csv

ci-bot: job 9766 finished. results: ndcg@10 delta -0.007 (p=0.11), mrr delta -0.013 (p=0.04). raw: https://internal.gdrive/redwood/9766_results.csv

ci-bot: job 9767 finished. results: float16 tiefix vs int4 tiefix: mrr float16=0.311, int4=0.295 (p=0.018). raw: https://internal.gdrive/redwood/9767_results.csv

anya: initial read — stripping priming reduced the gap a lot (9765 ns), shuffling candidates still shows some delta (9766), tie-fix didn't remove delta (9767). looks like both priming and candidate sampling interact with quant noise.

mike: sounds like a multi-factor effect. next steps: 1) run tokenization-length aware quant profile (eva), 2) increase bootstrap replicates to 5k for stability (sanjay), 3) add an eval with priming but smaller header (anya).

eva: i'll schedule the quant-profile run and send config.

sanjay: i'll re-run 9766 with 5k boots.

julian: also capture top-3 tie shifts per query to see whether order flips correlate with MRR drop. small diagnostic script can do that.

anya: will add that script to the eval harness and include per-query flip counts in the next CSV. thanks all. :thumbsup:
